title: User-research search-angle output
description: The output of ONE search angle. A discriminated union on `outcome`: an angle that did not run and an angle that ran and found nothing are different facts, and this schema refuses to let them look alike. Wave 1 — a candidate here is a SOURCE, not a finding; findings are minted inside the extract wave.

note.description: Run-level context. Without it such context is pushed into `notes`, which is scoped to cross-angle leads for the caller to route.

outcome.description: `not_run` — the angle's precondition failed. `vacated` — the precondition held but nothing was applicable. `ran` — the angle worked its cells. Only `ran` may carry coverage.

status_counts.description: One entry per cell status present in coverage, and the counts must reconcile against the cells themselves.

cap.description: The REGISTRY's cap for this angle. A run may neither raise its own ceiling nor quietly lower it.

dropped_note.description: Required when hit is true: what the cap dropped, IN KIND. 'Some results' is not a note.

reason.description: Why it was not carried forward. `abstract-only` is the commonest and must be stated as such — a source dropped silently makes 'we did not look' and 'we looked and it was not usable' indistinguishable one layer down.

notes.description: Cross-angle leads for the caller to route. Working another angle's channels inflates this angle's arithmetic and leaves the other's cells unexplained.

cell_status.description: `forbidden-by-terms` is a DELIBERATE non-fetch (the source's terms or robots forbid automated access), distinct from `unreachable`, which is a fetch that failed. Collapsing them hides a policy decision inside an outage. `rate-limited` is its own member because one of this survey's sources runs a globally shared unauthenticated pool, where throttling is a normal operating condition rather than an outage.

queries.description: EVERY query run for this pair, verbatim AS RUN — the central requirement of reproducible search, and the one routinely claimed and not delivered. A paraphrase cannot be re-run, and a coverage record that cannot be re-run proves nothing.

returned.description: Required when status is reached: the result count the source gave back.

kept.description: Required when status is reached: how many distinct candidate ROWS this cell carried forward into candidates plus unadmitted — NEVER a result count.

selection.description: Required when the registry declares a crawl delay for this source: how the shortlist was chosen from an index, and what was identified but deliberately not fetched. A delayed source crawled breadth-first spends the whole run on retrieval, so the selection IS the method for those cells and an unstated one cannot be judged.

candidate.description: ONE SOURCE — a paper, a report, an article — not a finding. How many findings a source contains is knowable only after the full read, so finding ids are minted in the extract wave and never appear here.

id_class.description: Governs the shape of id: DOI-<doi>, ARXIV-<id>, WEB-<domain>-<slug>. A DOI always contains '/', which is why the record filename is derived rather than taken from the id.

url.description: Required for id_class `web`, which has no resolver behind it.

found_by.description: The (group_id, source_id) cell this candidate came out of, written 'group/source'.

admission.description: Why this source was carried forward. THIS SURVEY'S OWN PREDICATE, and not the sibling surveys': a source is admitted only when its full text is retrievable without bypassing a paywall AND it states a method. Both conjuncts are load-bearing — full text without a stated method yields a record with nothing to weigh, and a stated method behind a paywall yields a record built from an abstract.

full_text_url.description: Where the full text was reached, without a paywall and without bypassing one.

method_stated.description: The study design as the source itself names it. Not your inference from its title — a title stating a result is not a method.
